title: Leading-eigenvalue approximation without a spectral gap: relative Rayleigh error.
summary: Find a unit vector $\widehat{v}$ such that $\widehat{v}^{\mathsf T}A\widehat{v}$ approximates $\lambda_1(A)$.

task.description_zh: Find a unit vector $\widehat v$ such that $\widehat v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat v$ approximates $\lambda_1(A)$.
description_paragraphs: Find a unit vector $\widehat{v}$ such that $\widehat{v}^{\mathsf T}A\widehat{v}$ approximates $\lambda_1(A)$.

model.instance: An unknown nonzero real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, with $\lambda_{\max}(A)>0$. No eigengap or simple-eigenvalue assumption is imposed.

assumptions.description: A is nonzero and positive semidefinite

model.parameter_domain_description: $d\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$; nontrivial accuracy and lower-bound regimes are stated separately.
model.description_zh: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$, $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, and $\lambda_1(A)>0$. The largest eigenvalue may have multiplicity greater than one.
description_paragraphs: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$, $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, and $\lambda_1(A)>0$; the largest eigenvalue may have multiplicity greater than one.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The dimension $d$ and tolerance $\varepsilon$ are public; $A$ is hidden. A query $v\in\mathbb R^d$ returns exact $Av$. Query vectors have unrestricted norm and may be adaptive or repeated.
description_paragraphs: The data $d,\varepsilon$ are public and $A$ is hidden. Any query $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns exact $Av$. Queries have no norm restriction and may be adaptive or repeated.

output.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return a unit vector $\widehat v\in\mathbb R^d$. It need not have been queried, and no additional estimate or certificate of the largest eigenvalue is required.
description_paragraphs: Return a unit vector $\widehat v\in\mathbb R^d$. It need not have been queried. No separate largest-eigenvalue estimate or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Rayleigh-objective gap normalized by positive $\lambda_{\max}(A)$, not an eigenvector angle.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: The base loss is $\ell(\widehat v)=(\lambda_1(A)-\widehat v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat v)/\lambda_1(A)$ and success requires $\ell\le\varepsilon$. Its denominator is positive under the nonzero positive-semidefinite promise.
description_paragraphs: The base loss is $\ell(\widehat{v})=(\lambda_1(A)-\widehat{v}^{\mathsf T}A\widehat{v})/\lambda_1(A)$ and success requires $\ell\le\varepsilon$. Its denominator is positive under the nonzero positive-semidefinite promise.

resource.budget_semantics: A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

proofs.title: Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task
proofs.body: Recover the $d$ columns of $A$ using standard basis queries. Exact internal eigendecomposition returns a unit vector for its largest eigenvalue, giving zero relative Rayleigh loss. No positive spectral gap is needed.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.supports: The lower bound covers arbitrary randomized adaptive matrix–vector queries on hard matrices of size s ≤ d at accuracy 1/(20s²). Fixed success probabilities can be converted at constant cost by independent repetition, followed by Rayleigh-value queries and selection of the best candidate.
